title: General-purpose LLMs as Models of Human Driver Behavior: The Case of Simplified Merging

live_model.evidence: "We evaluated two general-purpose LLM driver agents, OpenAI o3 (o3-2025-04-16) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (June 2025 release)"; Table III/IV/V report o3-specific regression coefficients and behavioral metrics.

prompt.location: Table II (prompt components C0-C5 and ablations A1-A7 described); "the full prompt text is provided in the supplementary online material"
prompt.note: In-paper text gives the component structure and ablation design, not the literal prompt string; full text is only in supplementary material, which is not part of this corpus.

claim.metric: mean gap at merge point (meters), o3 baseline prompt
claim.location: Sec III-A / Table V: "o3 maintains substantially larger gaps on average (9.28 m) than humans (3.85 m) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (3.84 m)"; n=109 o3 trials (baseline prompt, 11 kinematic conditions x 10 repetitions, minus excluded collisions/unfinished trials)

data.source: Simulated one-dimensional merging scenario; software, simulated data and supplementary info at https://github.com/shamohammad/General-purpose-LLM-Merging

notes: Clean dated snapshot, role S (o3 embedded as a standalone closed-loop driver agent), n=109 baseline trials plus 55 trials per each of 7 single-factor ablations (all public via GitHub). Soft gap keeping this at 'maybe' rather than 'eligible': the literal prompt text lives only in supplementary material not present in papers_tierb, only its component structure (Table II) is in the main text. Cost is likely underestimated at 500 calls since each trial may involve multiple re-planning calls across the interaction window; o-series pricing pushes this into the high tier regardless.
